importance_ranking.reason: Extreme visual variation across sub-types — a bamboo resort hut, a steel PUF labour quarter, and a GI sheet guard cabin are unrecognisable as the same category without an image. Buyers use the image to identify product type and construction quality before reading any text.

Structure material, wall panel type, size, and roof type are non-interchangeable shortlisting criteria. A buyer specifying PUF-insulated MS-frame huts for a desert site cannot substitute bamboo or GI sheet cladding — specs are the primary qualification gate.

Construction contractors compare per-sq-ft rates aggressively once material and panel type are confirmed. Price varies substantially across structure material tiers (bamboo vs MS PUF vs FRP), making it a primary decision lever after spec match.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard fixed-size models (10x10 ft, 8x20 ft) are also quoted per piece — unit must be shown to prevent price comparison errors between area-based and per-unit listings.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per piece is a documented market ambiguity for this MCAT. Price cannot be meaningfully compared across listings without knowing the unit basis.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category — market is fragmented across regional fabricators and buyers search by material, size, and price rather than manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: For large labour camp orders, buyers evaluate installation capability, service reach, and track record. Company matters as a post-shortlist qualifier but does not drive initial engagement.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the fundamental product class — MS/Steel PUF hut vs Bamboo vs FRP are non-interchangeable across buyer segments and carry the largest price delta in the category.
Within the steel-frame segment, PUF vs EPS vs GI sheet cladding drives significant price and thermal performance differences that are non-interchangeable for insulation-critical site applications.

missing_important_specs.why_important: PUF panel thickness (50mm / 75mm / 100mm) is a primary thermal and structural spec that buyers specify for climate-appropriate site accommodation — thicker panels command a significant price premium and are non-interchangeable for cold-region or desert deployments.

Single-room vs multi-room configuration is a fundamental procurement dimension for labour camp buyers — a 20-room labour colony and a single guard cabin are priced and fabricated entirely differently.
Government, EPC, and paramilitary buyers specify wind zone compliance (IS 875 Part 3) as a procurement requirement — sellers must confirm structural grade to be eligible for tender response.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to the correct seller type — bamboo/natural material fabricators vs steel/FRP manufacturers are entirely different supplier pools and cannot substitute for each other.
Tells sellers the use context (site office vs restaurant vs staff housing), which determines structural requirements, fire safety configuration, and product tier — enabling accurate quote generation.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need room count to determine whether the buyer needs a single portable unit or a multi-room modular labour camp — these require fundamentally different fabrication, logistics, and pricing.
